clean_source_blocks.text: Japanese islands like Ishigaki have borne the brunt of Typhoon Bavi as it powers through the Pacific Hundreds of thousands of people have been evacuated from areas of eastern China as a powerful typhoon - the country's second in a week - barrels towards the coast. Typhoon Bavi, which spans 1,000km (620 miles) at its widest point - roughly the width of France - is expected to make landfall near the major city of Wenzhou on Sunday morning. After pummelling a chain of remote Japanese islands, it brought heavy rainfall to Taiwan as it brushed past its northern tip. Earlier landslides triggered by the storm killed 17 people in the Philippines. Though it has weakened to a Category 1 typhoon, it still presents a risk because of the huge volume of moisture within its rain bands.
Hundreds of thousands of people are evacuated from eastern Zhejiang province, with the city of Wenzhou close to the path of the storm.

Bavi is forecast to bring "exceptionally heavy rains" to eastern Zhejiang province and northeastern Fujian province, the authorities said, adding that evacuations were "undertaken entirely to guard against the [worst-case] scenario". The city of Wenzhou, home to around 10 million people, is close to the path of the storm. Bavi began as a super typhoon, battering Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands last Monday with wind speeds of 290km/h (180mph). As it made its way through the Pacific, weakening to 144 km/h winds, it struck the Sakishima islands, part of Japan's Ryukyu island chain between the country's main islands and Taiwan. At least five people were injured and thousands were without power.

See more of our coverage in your search results. China evacuated more than 1.8 million people on Saturday ​as Typhoon Bavi churned toward the major eastern city of Wenzhou after pummelling Japan’s southern Sakishima island chain with heavy rain and violent ‌winds and brushing past northern Taiwan. Even as Bavi continues to slow and weaken on its northwesterly path over cooler seas, the typhoon is still a potent risk due to the sheer volume of moisture it holds within its rain bands, about the size of France from end to end. Bavi had maximum sustained winds of 90 mph, equivalent to Category 1 ​on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale, and was about 124 miles southeast of Wenling in the eastern province of Zhejiang as of 8:08 a.m., according to the National Meteorological Center.

payload.title: Kiina evakuoi yli 1,8 miljoonaa ihmistä taifuuni Bavin lähestyessä rannikkoa
payload.summary: Taifuuni Bavin odotetaan tuovan poikkeuksellisen voimakkaita sateita Itä-Kiinaan. Myrsky on heikentynyt, mutta sen laajat ja kosteutta sisältävät sadealueet aiheuttavat edelleen huomattavan vaaran.
payload.content:
Kiina on evakuoinut yli 1,8 miljoonaa ihmistä taifuuni Bavin lähestyessä maan itärannikkoa. Noin tuhannen kilometrin levyisen myrskyn odotetaan saapuvan maihin sunnuntaiaamuna lähellä Zhejiangin maakunnassa sijaitsevaa Wenzhoun suurkaupunkia. Kyseessä on toinen Kiinaa viikon sisällä lähestyvä taifuuni.

## Rankkasateisiin varaudutaan kahdessa maakunnassa

Viranomaiset ennustavat Bavin tuovan poikkeuksellisen voimakkaita sateita Zhejiangin itäosiin ja Fujianin koillisosiin. Evakuoinnit on heidän mukaansa toteutettu kokonaan pahimman mahdollisen tilanteen varalta. Noin kymmenen miljoonan asukkaan Wenzhou sijaitsee lähellä myrskyn arvioitua reittiä.

Bavi oli lauantaiaamuna kello 8.08 noin 200 kilometriä Zhejiangissa sijaitsevasta Wenlingistä kaakkoon, kertoi Kiinan kansallinen meteorologinen keskus. Myrskyn suurin jatkuva tuulennopeus oli tuolloin noin 144 kilometriä tunnissa, mikä vastaa ensimmäisen luokan taifuunia Saffirin–Simpsonin asteikolla.

Myrsky on hidastunut ja heikentynyt liikkuessaan luoteeseen viileämpien merialueiden yllä. Se muodostaa silti vakavan vaaran, koska sen laajoihin sadealueisiin on sitoutunut runsaasti kosteutta. Bavi ulottuu leveimmillään noin tuhannen kilometrin alueelle, mikä vastaa suunnilleen Ranskan leveyttä. Siksi heikentyneet tuulet eivät poista erittäin runsaiden sateiden riskiä.

## Bavi aiheutti vahinkoja Tyynenmeren saarilla

Bavi kehittyi aiemmin supertaifuuniksi ja koetteli maanantaina Guamia sekä Pohjois-Mariaaneja. Tuulen nopeus nousi tuolloin jopa 290 kilometriin tunnissa. Myrsky heikkeni myöhemmin edetessään Tyynellämerellä kohti Japanin Ryukyu-saariketjuun kuuluvaa Sakishiman saariryhmää, joka sijaitsee Japanin pääsaarten ja Taiwanin välissä.

Sakishiman saarilla Bavi toi voimakkaita tuulia ja rankkasateita. Ainakin viisi ihmistä loukkaantui, ja tuhannet jäivät ilman sähköä. Myrsky kulki myös Taiwanin pohjoiskärjen läheltä ja toi alueelle runsaita sateita ennen jatkamistaan kohti Kiinan rannikkoa.

Baviin liittyneet maanvyöryt surmasivat aiemmin Filippiineillä 17 ihmistä. Kiinassa huomio kohdistuu nyt Zhejiangin ja Fujianin sateisiin sekä Wenzhoun lähistölle ennustettuun maihinnousuun. Vaikka myrsky on heikentynyt voimakkaimmasta vaiheestaan, viranomaiset varautuvat edelleen sen sisältämän kosteuden ja laajan sadealueen seurauksiin.
summary_bullets: Yli 1,8 miljoonaa ihmistä on evakuoitu Itä-Kiinassa.
Taifuunin odotetaan saapuvan maihin lähellä Wenzhouta sunnuntaiaamuna.
Bavi on heikentynyt, mutta sen laajat sadealueet sisältävät yhä runsaasti kosteutta.

article.source_text:
Japanese islands like Ishigaki have borne the brunt of Typhoon Bavi as it powers through the Pacific Hundreds of thousands of people have been evacuated from areas of eastern China as a powerful typhoon - the country's second in a week - barrels towards the coast. Typhoon Bavi, which spans 1,000km (620 miles) at its widest point - roughly the width of France - is expected to make landfall near the major city of Wenzhou on Sunday morning. After pummelling a chain of remote Japanese islands, it brought heavy rainfall to Taiwan as it brushed past its northern tip. Earlier landslides triggered by the storm killed 17 people in the Philippines. Though it has weakened to a Category 1 typhoon, it still presents a risk because of the huge volume of moisture within its rain bands.

Hundreds of thousands of people are evacuated from eastern Zhejiang province, with the city of Wenzhou close to the path of the storm.

Bavi is forecast to bring "exceptionally heavy rains" to eastern Zhejiang province and northeastern Fujian province, the authorities said, adding that evacuations were "undertaken entirely to guard against the [worst-case] scenario". The city of Wenzhou, home to around 10 million people, is close to the path of the storm. Bavi began as a super typhoon, battering Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands last Monday with wind speeds of 290km/h (180mph). As it made its way through the Pacific, weakening to 144 km/h winds, it struck the Sakishima islands, part of Japan's Ryukyu island chain between the country's main islands and Taiwan. At least five people were injured and thousands were without power.

See more of our coverage in your search results. China evacuated more than 1.8 million people on Saturday ​as Typhoon Bavi churned toward the major eastern city of Wenzhou after pummelling Japan’s southern Sakishima island chain with heavy rain and violent ‌winds and brushing past northern Taiwan. Even as Bavi continues to slow and weaken on its northwesterly path over cooler seas, the typhoon is still a potent risk due to the sheer volume of moisture it holds within its rain bands, about the size of France from end to end. Bavi had maximum sustained winds of 90 mph, equivalent to Category 1 ​on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale, and was about 124 miles southeast of Wenling in the eastern province of Zhejiang as of 8:08 a.m., according to the National Meteorological Center.
